headword: お{願|ねが}いいたします

definitions.gloss: please; thank you in advance; if you would (very polite)
definitions.explanation: A very polite request expression formed by combining the humble verb いたす with the noun {願|ねが}い (request). Used to politely ask for help, action, or continued goodwill. More formal than the everyday お{願|ねが}いします.

examples.japanese: よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: I look forward to working with you (very polite).

examples.japanese: ご{確認|かくにん}のほどお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: I would appreciate your kind confirmation.

examples.japanese: {今後|こんご}とも{変|か}わらぬお{引|ひ}き{立|た}てを{賜|たまわ}りますよう、お{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: I respectfully ask for your continued patronage.

notes:
Replaces します with the humble form いたします to lift the politeness of お{願|ねが}いします a notch. Standard register for emails to clients, business letters, and formal customer service.

LEVELS OF "PLEASE":
- {頼|たの}む: casual; among friends, between equals
- お{願|ねが}い: casual to neutral; everyday request
- お{願|ねが}いします: standard polite; ubiquitous
- お{願|ねが}いいたします: very polite; humble form, business and formal contexts
- お{願|ねが}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます: extremely polite; ceremonial speeches and formal letters

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします: very polite "thank you in advance" / "nice to meet you"
- {何卒|なにとぞ}お{願|ねが}いいたします: "please, I humbly ask"
- ご{確認|かくにん}お{願|ねが}いいたします: "please confirm" (in business email)

NOTE:
Very common as a closing line in business emails, often combined with {何卒|なにとぞ} (please, kindly) for added formality.
